title: Run the first Next.js change window

bridge.applicationConcept: Branch, commit, pull request, preview, merge, and revert
bridge.analogyLimit: A pull request also validates user value, accessibility, and maintainability; it is not only an infrastructure change record.

buildBrief: Fork the program, open the onboarding Next.js lab in StackBlitz, change the operator handoff message through GitHub's web editor, create a focused branch, and submit the change through a pull request.
incidentBrief: A conflicting handoff edit and a harmless bad merged message simulate an unsafe change. Resolve the conflict, show the resulting diff, and use GitHub's Revert action without deleting history.
instructions: Create `lab-00-approved` and `lab-00-conflict` from the same unchanged `main` branch; edit the same handoff line differently on each branch through GitHub's web editor.
Preview a branch by replacing `/tree/main` in the StackBlitz URL with `/tree/BRANCH_NAME`; use its terminal for the baseline and incident commands.
Merge the approved PR first, open the conflict PR second, use GitHub's conflict editor to preserve the approved message, and explain each marker before committing the resolution.
Create and merge one separate harmless bad-message PR, then use its GitHub Revert action and merge the generated revert PR to restore the accepted message.

scenario.symptoms: The incident check reports a conflicting and unsafe handoff message.
scenario.reset: Use the merged pull request's Revert action and merge the generated revert pull request

acceptanceTests: The Next.js page renders the approved handoff message
The pull request shows coherent commits and a resolved conflict
A revert restores the last accepted behavior without rewriting history
evidence: Before, conflict, resolution, and revert screenshots
predictionQuestions: Which repository and branch will change after each action?
What history will remain after revert compared with deleting the commit?
defenseQuestions: Trace the change from browser edit to merged repository state.
Explain fork, clone, branch, commit, pull request, merge, and revert in your own words.
Show one controlled text change without asking Codex to regenerate the page.
hints: Draw the canonical repository, your fork, and the two browser branches as separate boxes before editing.
Compare both sides of the conflict marker and restate the desired final sentence.
Use a new commit that reverses the bad commit; do not erase shared history.
